page: Vultr voc-s-4c-32gb-960s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring an AMD EPYC processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, 2 physical cores, and 2 threads per core running at 2.0 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64, supported by 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled as a 960 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this instance.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the top 10%. Multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores fall in the average range. Memory performance is strong, with Passmark memory score and large-block write bandwidth ranking in the top 25%, though read bandwidth remains average. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks are strong, but multi-threaded decompression and database operations show weaker relative performance.

This hardware profile is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation and high single-core performance, such as caching layers, memory-optimized general-purpose applications, and moderate-scale data processing. However, the server exhibits weaker throughput in static web serving and multi-threaded decompression, indicating it is less optimal for high-concurrency web serving or heavy parallel database operations.
description: Vultr voc-s-4c-32gb-960s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, 2 physical cores, and a 2.0 GHz clock speed. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 32.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per core) and a bundled 960 GB NVMe SSD, with no GPU acceleration. Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core CPU capabilities and strong memory write bandwidth, though multi-core performance and database operations are average to weak. This resource configuration offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound applications that do not require extreme multi-threaded scaling. It is best suited for memory-intensive workloads, caching systems, and single-threaded processing tasks.
